claim: Page 727 lists so as among the prepositions heading purpose PPs: “The prepositions found here are in order (finite or infinitival), so (finite), so as (infinitival)”. Page 728 has “In subjectless clauses governed by in order or so as”.
evidence_summary: Ch. 14 p. 1262: “The only prepositional expressions that take to-infinitivals other than interrogatives as direct complement are purposive in order, and as if/though”. Ch. 14 p. 1264: “The as here is itself licensed by so or such.” Ch. 17 p. 1540 makes so the preposition and says its complement “can have the form of as + infinitival”, citing Ch. 8, §12.2.
finding: Medium confidence: Ch. 8 lists so as as a preposition taking an infinitival, which Ch. 14 p. 1262 rules out, while Chs. 14 and 17 make so the head and as + infinitival its complement. Page 728’s “Infinitivals governed by so + as” recognizes two words, but it still makes the infinitival a dependent of the pair.
inference: Is so as a preposition taking an infinitival complement?

evidence.passage: §12.2, p. 727. “The prepositions found here are in order (finite or infinitival), so (finite), so as (infinitival)”
evidence.establishes: The chapters assign the head of the purpose PP differently.
